Russian Missile and Drone Barrage Hits Odesa Region, Injuring 35 — Russian forces launched a massive missile and drone assault targeting the Odesa region early Saturday morning, Sept. 12, injuring at least 35 people in the regional capital and five others – including four children – in Chornomorsk. A residential fire engulfed multiple upper floors of a 25-story apartment building, while strikes damaged gas lines, private homes, and a rehabilitation facility.

US House to Vote Next Week on Graham’s Russia Sanctions Bill — The US House of Representatives will vote next week on a bipartisan Russia sanctions bill championed by Senator Lindsey Graham. Considered under simple-majority rules, the legislation authorizes US President Donald Trump to impose 100% tariffs on the five largest purchasers of Russian crude oil and natural gas, as well as on five nations facilitating sanctions evasion

Drones Strike Taganrog Airfield and Tolyatti Chemical Plant — Drone strikes early Saturday morning, Sept. 12, hit both the Taganrog-Tsentralny military airfield in Russia’s Rostov region and the KuibyshevAzot chemical plant in Tolyatti, Samara region. Detonations and thick smoke were recorded across the base housing Russia’s 708th Military Transport Aviation Regiment and the 325th Aircraft Repair Plant in Taganrog. In Tolyatti, drones sparked a major blaze at KuibyshevAzot, a vital defense suppl

Zelensky Warns of Reciprocal Strikes if Russia Targets Power Grid — President Volodymyr Zelensky warned that Ukraine will strike back symmetrically if Russia attacks its power grid this winter, pledging to respond in kind if Moscow induces blackouts. Speaking to Fareed Zakaria and at the Yalta European Strategy summit on Friday, Sept. 11, Zelensky advocated for a mutual “energy truce” to protect energy infrastructure on both sides alongside unblocking the Black Sea food corridor.

Russian Strikes Kill 3, Injure 5 in Kryvyi Rih and Kharkiv — Russian forces launched ballistic missiles and attack drones against Kryvyi Rih overnight Friday-Saturday, killing two people, leaving one missing, and injuring three, while damaging an industrial enterprise, five apartment buildings, a healthcare center, and three schools. The barrage followed a Friday evening drone strike on Kharkiv’s Kyivskyi district that killed a 32-year-old man and injured two others
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, September 11, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on September 11, 2026.

Russian Missile-Drone Attack Hits Odesa Apartment Building, Injures Six — A Russian missile and drone attack damaged a residential high-rise in Odesa early Saturday, injuring at least six people, all of whom were hospitalized.

Russian Official to Attend G20 Energy Talks in Houston Despite Previous EU Protests — A Russian official will attend G20 energy talks in Houston weeks after Moscow’s return to an in-person G20 meeting drew protests from European officials over the war in Ukraine.

Putin Admits Russia Is World’s Biggest Sanctions Target, Ramps Up Anti-West Rhetoric — In a BRICS speech and Q&A with Russian journalists, Putin attacked the G7, NATO and European leaders while portraying BRICS as a rising alternative to Western influence.

Putin Threatens Europe Over Possible Troop Deployment in Ukraine — Russian President Vladimir Putin issued another threat to Europe, warning that deploying troops to Ukraine would mean war with Russia, while simultaneously claiming Moscow poses no threat to the continent.
Russian Drone Strikes Zaporizhzhia Home, Killing Woman — A Russian drone destroyed a private home in Zaporizhzhia, killing a woman as Moscow continued aerial attacks across Ukrainian cities.

Ukraine’s Mahuchikh Makes History as First Ultimate High Jump Champion — Ukrainian Olympic champion and world record-holder Yaroslava Mahuchikh cleared 1.99 meters in Budapest to become the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate champion in women’s high jump

Zelensky Warns of Global Food Crisis, Urges Faster Sanctions on Russia — President Volodymyr Zelensky said Friday, Sept. 11, that Ukraine will not run out of food despite the Black Sea blockade. However, he warned that other nations could face severe shortages and urged for immediate US sanctions on Russia.

Hungary Fails in Lawsuit Over Use of Frozen Russian Assets for Ukraine — The European Court of Justice has dismissed Hungary’s lawsuit challenging the use of frozen Russian asset revenues for Ukraine’s military aid. The tribunal ruled it lacks jurisdiction over the matter. Hungary was excluded from allocation votes after constructively abstaining from initial decisions.

Medvedev: NATO Will Not Invoke Article 5 if Russia Strikes Lithuania — Dmitry Medvedev, former President and current Deputy Chairman of the Russian Security Council, threatened Lithuania would “disappear from the map of the world” in case of a conflict linked to Vilnius' nuclear weapons ban lift. He also claimed NATO would not invoke Article 5 to defend the country as that would mean a “global catastrophe.”

EU Fails to Extend Russia Sanctions For Second Time — EU ambassadors failed to agree on extending sanctions against Russia for a second time on Friday, Sept. 11, after France joined Slovakia in demanding the delisting of Russian-Uzbek oligarch Alisher Usmanov. The bloc will continue discussions on Monday, Sept. 14, just one day before the sanctions expire.

Russian Strikes Kill 6, Injure 33 in Nationwide Barrage on Ukraine — Russian forces launched a sweeping wave of strikes across Ukraine on Friday, Sept. 11, killing at least six people and injuring 33 others, including children. Drones, artillery and guided aerial bombs (KABs) struck Kyiv, Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Kirovohrad and several other regions.

Discount Terror: How Putin Gutted Russia’s Premier S-400 Systems — Chuck Pfarrer takes apart Russia’s newest weapon of desperation: the modified 48N6 variant of the premier S-400 anti-aircraft system.

Russia Launches First Commercial 5G Networks For First Time Since Nearly a Decade of Delays — Russia launched its first commercial 5G networks in 16 major cities on Friday, Sept. 11, reaching an estimated 10 million people. The rollout, ordered by Russian President Vladimir Putin, follows nearly a decade of delays caused by Western sanctions, equipment shortages and a dispute over frequency bands.

Russian Lawmaker Threatens New Oreshnik Strike on Ukraine — Russian State Duma lawmaker Andrey Kolesnik threatened Ukraine with another strike using the nuclear-capable Oreshnik ballistic missile, which has been used twice since November 2024. He claimed the weapon could be deployed if alleged Ukrainian attacks against Russian civilians intensified, citing recent operations against Novorossiysk and Sochi.

Russia Hits Kyiv’s Telecom Building Amid Widening Gas Station Strikes — Russian jet-powered Shahed drones struck a building belonging to Ukraine’s largest telecom company and deliberately targeted gas stations across Kyiv on Friday. Two people were killed and nine injured, including a rescuer wounded in a repeat strike. The attacks began overnight and affected Kyiv and eight Ukrainian regions.

Lukashenko Floats Mobilization, Says Attacking Neighbors Would Be ‘Tantamount to Death’ — Belarusian leader Alexander Lukashenko said readiness inspections would cover the entire army and could include mobilization. At the same time, he denied plans to attack neighboring countries, saying such a move would be “tantamount to death” because Belarus could not win a conflict against the powerful states surrounding it.

Same Appeasement, Same Mistakes — Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff visited Moscow and Kyiv on behalf of President Trump. Rather than making any progress toward peace, they exposed a rift in the administration that amounts to a fundamental weak spot in US foreign policy.

Ukraine Strikes Russian Aircraft Engine Plant, Pantsir Air Defenses – General Staff — Ukrainian forces struck a Russian defense plant producing aircraft engine components, along with Pantsir air defenses, a radar station and drone facilities across occupied territories and Russian regions, Kyiv’s General Staff said.

‘Weeks, Not Months’: Ukraine’s FP-7 Ballistic Missile Could Soon Strike Russia — Ukraine’s FP-7 tactical ballistic missile could enter combat within weeks after completing two testing stages, its manufacturer says. The 200-km weapon can carry a warhead of up to 150 kg, while Fire Point’s longer-range FP-9 is undergoing flight tests.

Putin's Wrong – Russia’s Oil Exports and Revenue Both Slump in August — Contrary to what Putin said in Vladivostok, it has not been more profitable for Russia to sell crude than to refine it domestically. August’s figures saw Russia’s overall exports dropping by 7% and revenue dropping by 8%, with seaborne crude revenues dropping 32% month-on-month, to a five-year low at $90 million per day.

EU Revives Push to Unlock Frozen Russian Assets for Ukraine — The European Commission is reviving efforts to use frozen Russian reserves to finance Ukraine, exploring a new structure designed to overcome Belgium’s objections. The push comes as Kyiv faces a $27 billion defense funding gap and mounting pressure from Russia’s intensified attacks.

‘Russia Will Feel It Firsthand’: Budanov Warns of Deeper Ukrainian Strikes — Presidential Office Chief Kyrylo Budanov warned that Ukrainian strikes inside Russia would become deeper and more powerful if Moscow continued the war. He said Kyiv was prepared to end hostilities with security guarantees and without legally recognizing Russia’s occupation of Ukrainian territory.

How 9/11 Changed America and Tested NATO’s Article 5 — The Sept. 11 attacks killed 2,977 people, transformed American security, and began two decades of war. They also provided NATO’s only test of Article 5. Allies defended US airspace and later deployed tens of thousands of troops, but each government retained control over what it contributed. That distinction remains critical for Ukraine.

Ukraine Is Losing Its Tech Edge to Russia, Former Google CEO Says — Ukraine’s technological advantage over Russia is rapidly diminishing as Moscow combines mass weapons production with faster battlefield innovation, former Google CEO Eric Schmidt warned. He said Ukraine lacks the industrial capacity to produce and deploy its technologies at scale and urged Western governments to supply more interceptors, ammunition and long-range weapons while investing directly in Ukrainian defense manufacturin

Russia's Jet Fuel Crisis Worsens as Airports Impose Refueling Restrictions — Russian media Vertska said it found at least 26 major Russian airports imposing refueling restrictions as the jet fuel crisis worsens; 15 impose them only on foreign airlines, and airports in southern Russia are most affected, as the region is frequently targeted by Ukrainian strikes.

Russia Sends Bones of Medieval Warrior to Ukraine Front to Boost Morale — A fragment of the right hand of Dmitry Donskoy, a medieval prince celebrated for his 1380 victory over the Golden Horde, will be displayed to Russian units along the front line.

Russia Issues Nuclear Threats to Lithuania Over Vilnius’s Plan to Lift Nuke Ban — After Vilnius moved one step closer to lifting the country’s longstanding nuke ban, the Kremlin said the country would be in the Russian nuclear weapons’ crosshairs, despite Moscow having begun deploying nuclear weapons in neighboring Belarus back in 2023.

EU Approves €6.1 Billion Ukraine Defense Package, Unlocking PAC-3 Patriot Purchases — EU approved a €6.1 billion defense package for Ukraine, allowing Kyiv to purchase US-made PAC-3 Patriot interceptors amid a global shortage. The decision also unlocks funding for Ukrainian drones and comes as Ukraine prepares for another winter of Russian strikes on its energy infrastructure.

Russia’s Recruitment of Foreign Fighters for Ukraine War ‘Amounts to Human Trafficking’ — Amnesty says Russia’s recruitment of foreign nationals to fight in Ukraine amounts to human trafficking, using deception and coercion. FIDH estimates more than 27,000 recruits from more than 130 countries. Testimonies describe false jobs, forced enlistment, and abuse.

India Welcomes Russia, Iran Leaders for BRICS Summit Overshadowed by War — Russia, Iran, China and India are set to take center stage at the BRICS summit in New Delhi, with the wars in Ukraine and the Middle East, oil and global trade tensions topping the agenda as Xi Jinping makes his first India visit since 2019.

9/11: 25th Anniversary of the Twin Towers Attacks — The article examines the lasting consequences of 9/11, arguing that the attacks transformed global security and US foreign policy. European commentators link the “War on Terror” to increased Islamophobia, anti-Americanism, weakened US democratic leadership, and the rise of populist movements, including Donald Trump’s MAGA politics.

Ukraine’s IMF Review Delayed Until December as Tax Reforms Stall, Source Says — Ukraine’s second IMF review has been pushed to December and will be combined with the third, delaying the next disbursement, a government source told Kyiv Post. IMF staff met opposition lawmakers during their September visit to discuss the legislative deadlock. Ukraine also faces a $32.6 billion financing gap for 2027 as Russian attacks raise costs and political resistance complicates efforts to secure more European

Polish Foreign Minister Sikorsky Arrives in Kyiv — Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorsky arrived in Kyiv on Friday, Sept. 11. His visit comes amid intensified Russian attacks on Ukraine and growing warnings from Warsaw about threats to Ukrainian-Polish border crossings.

St. Petersburg Metro Prepares 9 Stations as Civil Defense Shelters — St. Petersburg is preparing nine metro stations, four underground sections and 35 kilometers of tracks for use as civil defense shelters, with systems designed to filter radioactive dust, aerosols and toxic substances amid growing concerns over attacks and emergencies.

Russia Hits Kyiv Gas Stations for Second Straight Day, 2 Killed — Two people were killed and four others remained hospitalized after Russian drones struck gas stations in Kyiv’s Dniprovskyi and Obolonskyi districts on Friday morning. One gas station in Obolon was hit twice, while drone debris fell on a car nearby. The attack came hours after an overnight strike injured eight people, leaving one in serious condition.

Russian Chemical Giant’s Plant in Perm Targeted in Ukrainian Drone Strike — A major chemical plant in Russia’s Perm region was reportedly targeted by Ukrainian drones on Sept. 11. The attack on the Azot plant in Berezniki came amid a broader wave of strikes on Russian industrial infrastructure, including refineries and Ozon logistics hubs.

Kryvolap: His Journey, Ukraine’s Colors, Freedom, War, and Art — Anatoly Kryvolap is one of Ukraine’s best-known artists, whose works have topped international auction sales of Ukrainian art. Ahead of his 80th birthday, he spoke to Kyiv Post about his artistic journey, freedom, war, supporting the Ukrainian Armed Forces, and Ukraine’s future.

Russian Civilians Face Strain as Hospitals Prioritize Troops Wounded in Ukraine — At least 11 Russian regions have spent 3.2 billion rubles ($40 million) treating wounded troops in civilian facilities since 2022. Military patients are increasingly prioritized, while 19 regions plan to cut healthcare spending by nearly 107 billion rubles ($1.27 billion) in 2026.

Russia Attacks Kyiv, Zaporizhzhia With Drones, Injuring at Least 10 — Russia attacked Ukraine with 161 Shahed-type, Gerber and other drones overnight, injuring at least 10 people in Kyiv and Zaporizhzhia. Air defenses shot down or suppressed 138 drones, while strikes hit 19 locations.

Fires, Explosions Reported Across Russia as Ukrainian Drones Target Refineries, Ozon Hubs — Fires and explosions were reported at an oil refinery and an Ozon logistics center in Saratov, while industrial and residential sites were damaged in Volgograd, as Russian regions reported a new wave of overnight drone and missile attacks on Sept. 11.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, September 10, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on September 10, 2026.

Zelensky Says No Three-Way Peace Talks Until Russian Elections, Warns Moscow Escalates Attacks During Diplomacy — Zelensky says major Ukraine-Russia-US talks are unlikely before Russia’s elections and warns Moscow intensifies attacks whenever diplomacy advances.

Expelled Kremlin Propagandist’s TV Return Could Trigger Criminal Charges in France — France has warned CNews against putting former RT France chief Xenia Fedorova back on air after her expulsion over Kremlin-linked influence activity.

Zelensky Says He Plans to Meet Trump in New York in Late September — Zelensky says he expects to meet Donald Trump in New York later this month, while Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney says he has also recently discussed Ukraine with the US president.

What Putin Hopes to Gain From BRICS in India – and Why He May Not Get It — Putin is looking to BRICS for economic protection, diplomatic support and a stronger anti-Western front, but divisions over Ukraine, Iran and China limit Moscow’s ambitions.

Canada Pledges Over $2B in Air Defense, First Drone Deal Signed — President Volodymyr Zelensky said Thursday, Sept. 10, that Canada pledged more than $2 billion in new support for Ukraine, including over $1 billion for defense. The package includes urgently needed Patriot missiles, F-16 ammunition, and energy cooperation.

Poland Expects Russia to Target Its Border Crossings With Ukraine — Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Thursday, Sept. 10, that Poland expects Russia to target its border crossings with Ukraine after averting an overnight threat. He cited a similar drone strike on a Ukraine-Moldova crossing, and said the CIA reports warn of “possible events” on the eastern flank.

Zelensky Signs Historic 100-Year Partnership Agreement With Carney, Advances Drone Deal, FREYJA Support — President Volodymyr Zelensky met with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Thursday, Sept. 10, opening a three-day visit focused on winter support, energy, and air defense. The two signed a 100-year partnership agreement in Calgary, while Canada also agreed to join Ukraine’s FREYJA missile defense initiative with its technology.

Massive Russian Air Strikes Hit Kyiv and Regions, Killing 7, Injuring More Than 120 — A sweeping Russian aerial assault killed seven people and wounded more than 120 across Ukraine before fresh strikes hit Kyiv early Friday.

Business Centers Struck in Kyiv as Russia Escalates Drone Campaign — Preliminary reports suggest damage in Kyiv’s Obolonskyi and Solomyanskyi districts on Thursday evening as Russia steps up its drone campaign against Kyiv.

11 Wounded, Including 3 Children, as Russia Strikes Sumy — Russian forces struck a Sumy residential area with two guided aerial bombs (KABs) on Thursday, Sept. 10, injuring 11 people, including three children. The city’s mall Manufactura was hit for the second time after a drone struck it on Wednesday, Sept. 9, killing two people and injuring 20 others.

Russia Kills 2 Azeris in Tugboat Attack Off Odesa Coast — Baku and Kyiv confirmed that a Wednesday attack on a tugboat near southern Ukraine’s Odesa killed two Azeri crew members and hospitalized two more. Another similar incident took place in June, with Moscow pinning the blame on Kyiv both times despite conducting the attacks.

Why Germany Is Sounding Sirens Nationwide – Why Ukrainians React Differently — Germany conducted its sixth nationwide Warntag drill, testing sirens, phone alerts, television, radio, and other warning systems. While Germans largely treated the exercise as routine, Ukrainians living there described a more emotional response shaped by the war.

Ukraine’s ‘Sudden’ Victory in Lyman-Kharkiv: 5 Things to Know — Ukraine’s Lyman counteroffensive reclaimed up to 250 sq km, pushed Russian forces back toward the Zherebets River and threatened to isolate units. The months-long, drone-led operation exposed weaknesses in Russian defenses and command.

Ukraine Says It Hit 3 Russian Warships in Novorossiysk and Struck Caspian Sea Port — Ukrainian forces struck at least three Russian naval vessels and fuel-oil storage facilities in Novorossiysk on Wednesday, the General Staff said. A separate overnight attack caused a fire at the Makhachkala port, a key hub on Russia’s logistics route with Iran.

Alexei Ratmansky Has Staged Balanchine’s ‘Donizetti Variations’ in Kyiv — The production of George Balanchine’s “Donizetti Variations” by Alexei Ratmansky will be the first certified staging of Balanchine’s choreography for a Ukrainian ballet company. The project brings Ratmansky back to the National Opera of Ukraine, where his career began, after decades abroad.

Russia Sets Eye on Zaporizhzhia's Orikhiv With 150,000-Troop Formations — Russia is said to have amassed 120 assault formations, including 150,000 troops, near the city of Orikhiv in southern Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia region. A Ukrainian military press officer said the situation is difficult but under control, while noting that the widening kill zone has threatened Ukrainian logistics.

Moldova Accuses Russia of Deliberate Border Strike — Moldova accused Russia of deliberately striking the Tudora-Starokozache border crossing and trying to justify the attack with false claims that weapons pass through Moldova to Ukraine. Two Ukrainian civilians were killed, several people – including a Moldovan citizen – were injured, and operations at the border crossing were suspended.

SBU Foils FSB Plot to Kill Activist on Dog Walk — Ukraine said it thwarted an FSB-ordered assassination of a prominent civic activist in Kyiv region. A 19-year-old suspect allegedly tracked the target’s daily routine, retrieved a silenced pistol from a cache and prepared to ambush the activist during a morning dog walk. He faces possible life imprisonment.

Romania Rules Out Troop Deployments to Ukraine — Romania’s Presidential Administration said the country has no intention of fighting Russia in Ukraine after rumors claiming it plans to do so. In the same statement, it also ruled out troop deployments to Ukraine for postwar guarantees, and said only up to 20 officers might partake in the operational command based in Paris and London.

Russia Steps Up Deadly Attacks on Ukraine’s Passenger Trains — Russian attacks on four Ukrainian trains killed at least three people and injured 20 others over two days. Railway crews increasingly stop trains and evacuate passengers in remote areas when monitoring teams detect drones approaching.

Russia Turns to Vietnam for Aircraft as Sanctions Ground Hundreds of Planes — Russia is seeking a wet-lease deal with Vietnam to obtain aircraft, crews, and maintenance for Russian airlines. Moscow has approached several countries as sanctions and spare-parts shortages leave hundreds of Russian aircraft grounded.

Russia Hits Same Dnipro Plant Twice, Killing 2 — Two people were killed and two wounded when Russia struck the same food industry facility in Dnipro for a second time on Thursday. The deadly attack followed an earlier strike that damaged the enterprise without causing casualties, while overnight Russian attacks elsewhere in the Dnipropetrovsk region injured eight people.

Ukraine Hits Russian Oil, Port Infrastructure in Strikes Stretching From Arctic to Caspian — President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukrainian forces struck eight Russian infrastructure sites supporting Moscow’s war in a single day. The attacks stretched from an oil refinery in the Arctic Yamalo-Nenets region to the Makhachkala port on the Caspian Sea, which Ukraine says Russia used to import Iranian Shahed drones.

Kyiv Shortens Curfew, Changes Metro Rules as Russian Drone Attacks Intensify — Kyiv has shortened its curfew and introduced tighter rules for public transport, bridges and public events as Russia steps up drone attacks on the capital. The new measures include changes to metro operations during air alerts and special transport arrangements for passengers caught out by the curfew.

Ukraine Names New Leaders of Donetsk Military Groups — Ukraine has named two revamped military groupings within the Donetsk region where Brig. Gen. Biletsky will lead Center, and Brig. Gen. Prokopenko is expected to head Azov.

FSB Accuses Kyiv of Planning Attack on British Ambassador to Moscow — Russia’s FSB published a video of the interrogation of a Russian citizen who worked as a security officer at the British Embassy in Moscow. In it, he appears to confess that he had passed intelligence to a Ukrainian handler intended to be used in an attack on the ambassador.

SBU Unit Chief Detained Over Ammunition Storage Violations After 35 Killed Near Kyiv — The head of a Ukrainian Security Service unit has been placed in custody over alleged ammunition storage violations in Mila, Kyiv region. A Russian drone strike on the site on Aug. 28 triggered explosions that killed 35 people, injured 21, and left one person missing.

Russian Drone Strikes State-Owned Ukrnafta Gas Station in Kyiv, Smoke Seen Over City — A Russian drone fell onto a gas station in Kyiv’s Holosiivskyi district on Thursday, Sept. 10, sparking a fire and setting one car ablaze. Mayor Vitalii Klitschko said three people were injured and receiving medical treatment.

Xi Jinping’s September of Summits — While China seeks to maintain its role as the leading economic partner and strategic competitor for the US, the program of meetings planned by Beijing in September indicate Xi Jinping’s push to act within a multipolar world.

How ‘Call Centers’ Helped Bring Down Ukraine’s Prosecutor General — Kyiv Post takes a detailed look at the NABU "Carthage" operation. We explain what lies behind Prosecutor General Kravchenko’s resignation, and why it is connected to sinister call centers whose activities have been felt globally.

3,200 km Into Russia: Ukraine Hits 2 Major Gas Facilities in Record-Breaking Strike — Ukraine’s SSO said they struck the Novy Urengoy and Purovsky gas-condensate plants in Russia’s Yamalo-Nenets region. The drones traveled more than 3,000 kilometers, marking what Ukraine called its deepest strike of the war.

Polish FM Sees Little Hope for Ukraine Peace Talks as Putin Holds Out — Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski expressed little optimism about Ukraine peace talks, saying Russia continues to reject ceasefire proposals and pursue its existing goals. He urged stronger support for Ukraine’s military capabilities, while warning that Poland and Latvia face growing Russian hybrid threats, including airspace violations, migration pressure and sabotage.

Ukraine’s International Reserves Fall 5% to $48.7 Billion in August — Ukraine's international reserves dropped slightly to $48.7 billion in August. Despite heavy central bank interventions to stabilize the hryvnia, current reserves remain sufficient to cover four months of future national imports. Ukraine also received the USL loan tranche.

Ousted Defense Minister Fedorov Says Ukraine to Create Largest Defense Tech Fund — Ousted Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov says Ukraine will soon launch its largest Defense Tech venture fund. The initiative will back military startups developing battlefield robotics, air-defense interceptors and low-cost missiles.

Zelensky Arrives in Canada for Three-Day Visit Focused on Defense, Energy — Zelensky arrived in Canada for a three-day visit focused on boosting defense, economic and energy cooperation. Talks are expected to include ballistic missile defense, a key vulnerability for Ukraine as Russia continues its long-range missile and drone attacks.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, September 9, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on September 9, 2026.

Massive Russian Drone Assault Hits 5 Locations in Kryvyi Rih, Injuring 5 — Five people were injured in an overnight Russian drone attack on Kryvyi Rih. Two were hospitalized, including a 42-year-old man in serious condition.

Zelensky’s Drone-Disrupted Flight Highlights Wartime Travel Risks as Kyiv Calls Near-Miss Claims Exaggerated — A Russian drone incursion delayed Zelensky’s departure from Moldova, highlighting the security risks surrounding his extensive wartime travel and the sharp contrast with Putin’s much more limited foreign trips.

Russian Drone Strike on Sumy Shopping Center Kills 2, Injures at Least 20 — A Russian drone struck Sumy’s Manufaktura shopping center, killing a 21-year-old man and woman and injuring at least 20 people, including three teenagers.

Kim Jong Un Publicly Praises North Korean Troops Fighting for Russia — Kim Jong Un praised troops serving in “overseas military operations” during North Korea’s founding anniversary, publicly normalizing a deployment that has sent an estimated 14,000 to 15,000 soldiers to support Russia’s war against Ukraine.

PACE Panel Backs Using €260B in Russian Assets for Ukraine’s Legal Claims — PACE lawmakers have backed a proposal to use frozen Russian Central Bank assets to fund potentially billions in compensation for Ukraine under Strasbourg Court rulings.
